sources.title: Adverse effects of 21 antidepressants on sleep during acute-phase treatment in major depressive disorder: a systemic review and dose-effect network meta-analysis
sources.conciseFinding: This review compares treatment-emergent insomnia and somnolence across antidepressants; those harms cannot by themselves prove therapeutic benefit for pre-existing insomnia.

supportingSummary: Sleep can be a real fit dimension, but the trace must say whether the rule concerns improvement of an authored sleep problem or avoidance of a medication-emergent sleep harm.
opposingOrQualifyingSummary: Sedation is not a synonym for restorative sleep treatment. The context reviews cover different outcomes, time horizons, medications, and study designs and do not authorize a universal insomnia bonus.
proposedDirection: Keep baseline sleep findings and medication-emergent sleep risks as separate predicates. Consider a small positive fit direction only when the patient has a relevant authored sleep problem and the selected medication has reviewed therapeutic support; separately show sedation, somnolence, insomnia, and weight risks. Leave the active mirtazapine modifier and its magnitude provisional.
limitations: Zhang 2026 is publisher-copyrighted and remains abstract-only until a formal source-use review.
Zhou 2023 and its 2026 affiliation correction still need formal evidence and correction records before derived use.
The sources do not establish the same benefit for every kind of sleep complaint.
This packet authorizes no modifier or point change.

sources.title: The effects of antidepressants on cardiometabolic and other physiological parameters: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
sources.conciseFinding: Across short acute-treatment studies, the abstract reports meaningful between-drug physiological differences, including average weight direction; it does not establish long-term diabetes outcomes or deterministic individual response.

supportingSummary: A reviewed average weight-direction difference may support a small preference-sensitive fit modifier among otherwise acceptable treatments.
opposingOrQualifyingSummary: Short-term study-level averages do not prove that high BMI changes an individual's medication effect, that a medication causes a specific long-term diabetes outcome, or that either choice is absolutely contraindicated.
proposedDirection: Review medication-associated weight direction as one modest traceable dimension. Keep BMI, current weight trajectory, diabetes, long-term metabolic risk, appetite symptoms, and patient preference as separate facts or later rules. Do not approve the current high-BMI or diabetes modifiers, and do not treat a weight concern as a contraindication from this packet.
limitations: The Pillinger record is not yet admitted to the formal evidence and source-use catalogs.
Median follow-up in the review was short and the populations extended beyond uncomplicated adult MDD.
Study-level meta-regression must not become a deterministic patient-level modifier.
No point direction or magnitude is authorized.
unresolvedQuestions: Is average short-term weight direction sufficient for a small preference modifier?
What additional evidence is needed for BMI- or diabetes-specific rules?
Which authored patient facts should make weight direction clinically relevant rather than automatically scored?

sources.title: Screening for thyroid dysfunction and treatment of screen-detected thyroid dysfunction in asymptomatic, community-dwelling adults: a systematic review
sources.conciseFinding: The review found no direct studies of population screening and limited benefit evidence for treating screen-detected subclinical hypothyroidism; its asymptomatic screening population does not resolve targeted testing for a symptomatic psychiatric presentation.

supportingSummary: TSH can be defensible when authored facts create a targeted contributor question, and a clinically appropriate normal result should not lose credit merely because it is normal.
opposingOrQualifyingSummary: The current evidence does not support an undifferentiated routine laboratory panel or establish that every depressive presentation requires TSH. Population-screening evidence is not the same as case finding in a patient with a coherent thyroid history, examination finding, medication exposure, or symptom cluster.
proposedDirection: Present one reviewer choice: make TSH optional and defensible with no omission penalty in uncomplicated depression, then separately decide whether fatigue plus weight gain in this exact patient is enough to make it high-yield. Reserve strong reusable indications for explicit thyroid history or treatment, abnormal thyroid examination, thyroid-affecting medication, autoimmune or strong family history, or a reviewed coherent multi-feature syndrome. Do not change the current rule or points.
limitations: The Reyes Domingo record requires formal evidence and source-use intake before derived use.
The packet does not establish an exact symptom-count trigger.
Fatigue and modest weight change are nonspecific and need psychiatrist review in the authored context.
Testing cost and clinical correctness remain separate.

sources.title: Combining Antidepressants vs Antidepressant Monotherapy for Treatment of Patients With Acute Depression: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
sources.conciseFinding: The pooled trials found some antidepressant combinations could outperform monotherapy on average, which contradicts a blanket rule that any two antidepressants are automatically a dangerous combination.

supportingSummary: Treatment intent and treatment stage are necessary to explain why two selected medications represent supported combination, adjunctive treatment, a transition, duplicate therapy, or shotgun prescribing.
opposingOrQualifyingSummary: Evidence that some combinations can be effective does not make every pair useful or safe. A specific interaction, contraindication, duplicate role, unsupported initial strategy, and avoidable complexity remain separate evaluable problems.
proposedDirection: Require explicit categorical regimen intent in the future normalized regimen model. Retain a strong case-specific parsimony consequence for starting several same-role treatments when unsupported, but reserve reusable safety labels and score caps for an actual reviewed interaction, contraindication, duplication hazard, or case-supported danger. Do not revise the prototype safety rule from this packet.
limitations: Henssler 2022 does not identify every useful or safe pair and remains abstract-level context.
This packet does not define the normalized regimen schema or point values.
Intent alone cannot override pair-specific safety.
The current low-level patient may still forbid multi-start treatment as a case-design decision.
